about: Procedural course pieces for Stage D (SPEC §7.11). Ranges are [low, high], drawn evenly. Lengths in m, angles in degrees, impulses in N·s and N·m·s. run_out_m is flat floor kept after a piece (the landing zone) before the next checkpoint. Kept to what the driver bot with PD finishes: curved ramps up to 18° and 8-10 m wide, kickers 3.5-4.5 m wide so an off-centre car still gets both wheels on, gentle bumps, gaps the car clears at 10 m/s. Corkscrews (unaided they roll the car past 90°) and flip plates make Stage D flip the car for the thrusters to save. A flip plate is a game device, a kick plate whose impulses come from a named preset (world frame, for courses along +X) scaled by strength: front and back flips, barrel rolls each way, a roof toss that lands on the roof unaided, and a flat spin (weight 0 here: it lands the car facing sideways, which fails Stage D's heading rule; hand-made courses use it). strength is the mild range generated courses draw (the thrusters catch those flips early; with PD, Stage D succeeds 98% on 300 validation seeds); strong_strength is for hand-made courses and turns the car over even with the thrusters on. Walls are off (weight 0): their 30° ramp throws a car going over 20 m/s about 10 m up, and PD crashes most of those landings.
